title: canadian dollar edges lower trade war with us intensifies 2026 09 09
text:
TORONTO, Sept 9 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar weakened against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday as an escalating trade war between the ​United States and Canada offset higher oil prices, while bond ‌yields climbed.
The loonie was trading 0.2% lower at 1.3805 per U.S. dollar, or 72.44 U.S. cents, giving back much of the previous day's gains. It moved ​in a range of 1.3767 to 1.3820.
